gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
My brother and I ___ turns washing up after dinner.
gaps.explanation: take turns means to do something one after another, alternating.

gaps.sentence: Try to ___ quiet — the exam is in progress.
gaps.explanation: keep quiet means to stay silent; 'make quiet' is not used.

gaps.sentence: It gets bitterly ___ here in January.
gaps.explanation: bitterly cold is the fixed collocation for extremely cold weather.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the party.
gaps.explanation: have fun / have great fun is the fixed collocation; 'made fun' means mocked someone.
